correctness.rationale: The definitions and all ranges m>=3, n->infinity are explicit. The absorbing-race calculation gives exact petal avoidance probabilities under true nonbacktracking, including the forced second outer vertex; exact independent rational-state calculations pass 114 comparisons for m=2..7. The hub-memory correction is bounded at O(n^-2) per tagged-set excursion after conditional survival: the chance the prior incoming vertex was in one of finitely many marked petals is O(1/n). Factorial moments yield the Poisson uncovered-site limit, concentration of exponential-tailed excursion lengths yields edge-step Gumbel convergence, and a uniform one-site hazard union bound plus Wald yields expected cover times. Monte Carlo is not substituted for analytic proof. No result is claimed for growing m.

originality.rationale: The sharpened finding is a fixed-m>=3 cover-time Gumbel distribution and an explicit nonbacktracking-to-simple mean ratio on clique windmills. Published random-regular cover-time theory is nonapplicable at the n-dependent-degree hub, nonbacktracking Kemeny results concern a different invariant, and finite-chain rationality does not provide a sharp limit. The exact triangle-bouquet case m=2, previously established separately, is excluded rather than repackaged. No implication-equivalent result was identified in the actual literature/index and accessible-history comparisons; independent historical priority is not certified.
residual_risks: Historical priority is not independently certified; niche earlier cover-time analyses or book chapters could contain an equivalent fixed-m windmill formula.
The general bounded-degree vertex-transitive Gumbel paper was scope-screened at abstract level, not comprehensively read; its stated hypotheses are inapplicable.
Only fixed m>=3 is proved; extending to m growing with n requires new uniform estimates.

value.rationale: For a natural windmill family, a central hub presents a distinctive bottleneck, and each clique excursion has equal mean duration under both walks. The exact marked-petal avoidance laws show how nonbacktracking explores cliques more effectively; the genuinely dependent hub-excursion process nonetheless has Poisson last-site statistics and a sharp Gumbel law. The exact leading expected speedup (m+1)/(m+2) is an object-specific natural invariant, not just an exercise in applying an unrestricted coupon collector or a numerically tiny arbitrary perturbation.
